**Version · epoch:** viola-0.2.0 · Epoch 3 — Driver reliability: turns and sends.

1. **A trim-tolerant send match.** A driver's send whose text the CLI submits with whitespace trimmed is matched to
   the in-flight send: the `prompt-submitted` line is relabelled `driver`, the send is confirmed (`ok`), the wheel
   stays with the driver, and a later driver send is not refused for the wheel. The match tolerates exactly the
   whitespace the CLI trims, no more: a prompt differing in any other byte claims nothing, as today.
   `[inferred]` The comparison is `SendSlot::claim` (`src/run/send/slot.rs:78`, `f.text == text`), fed by
   `append_hook_event`; the relabel and the human wheel move sit in the same file and `src/run/send/relabel.rs`.

2. **Validated as received, never stripped.** The driver's text is validated as received (`validate_paste_text`:
   a C0 other than LF/CR/TAB, DEL or C1 is refused `not-delivered` / `control-character`, never removed), and viola
   types it without removing the whitespace the CLI will trim: the typed text keeps today's rules
   (`viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text`, CR LF and CR as one LF, trailing CR and LF not typed) and nothing else is
   taken off. An empty typed text stays `empty-text`. `[inferred]` Whether a text made only of the whitespace the
   CLI trims (but not empty after `typed_text`) needs its own decision is P3's to read and P4's to decide.

3. **The readiness-gate turn race closed.** A turn that starts while a send waits on the pre-send readiness gate
   (the settled-input-box predicate) never receives the send's text: the send is refused `turn-running`, or typed
   only once that turn has ended; a test reproduces the race. `[inferred]` The gate, the in-flight slot and the
   turn rung live in `src/run/send.rs` and `src/run/send/slot.rs`; where the window between the rung check and the
   paste lies is P3's to read.

4. **Capabilities this chunk addresses:** `v2-18` (whitespace the CLI trims, confirmed as the driver's own; a
   refused character still refused) and `v2-19` (a turn starting while a send waits on the readiness gate never
   receives the text; a test reproduces the race). Claims are decided at P5.

# Forks — 2026-11-16-send-confirmation, phase P4

The operator is away (directive `inputs#I1`, item 6): no dialog is raised. Q1 is the founder's, a boundary widening
under the playbook's escalate rules `rul-r74hshif` and `rul-p2zl2kgl` (a validated surface admits a new input
class); a delegate's answer to it lands PROVISIONAL, the founder's own word owed. Q2 is technical, answered by relay
at once. The phase stops here until the answer arrives; it is appended below, snapped and cited.

## Q1 (founder's) — how far the send's claim tolerates whitespace

Today `SendSlot::claim` (`src/run/send/slot.rs:83`) relabels a `prompt-submitted` `driver` only when its text equals
the send's typed text exactly; the security plan states it as «no tolerance on the submitted side»
(security-plan · decision/delivery-confirmation-exact-match). On claude 2.1.296 a send ending in a space was
submitted trimmed, missed the claim, was filed `human`, took the wheel, ended exit 13 and stranded every later send
until a `release` (`inputs#I1`). No recorded fixture set shows what the CLI trims (none ends a prompt in whitespace;
no 2.1.325 set exists). Matrix `v2-18` asks that such a send is confirmed as the driver's own. Every option keeps
the typed text as it is (nothing stripped), refused characters refused, the local-command list exact, harness
classification on the raw start, and a human's own different prompt still taking the wheel.

1. **(Recommended) Whitespace at either end.** The claim takes `S` when `S == T`, or when `S` is not empty and `T`
   is `S` with only whitespace before and after it (Unicode whitespace, `char::is_whitespace`). Why it wins: it
   holds whatever end trim the CLI does on any build, the untrimmed text included, so no send relies on the trim
   and no ledger row or live reading is needed (architecture decision/no-probe-for-unrelied-shapes); a prompt

   send's text up to end whitespace, filed `driver` inside that send's 10 s window.
2. **Trailing whitespace only.** The claim takes `S` when `S == T`, or `S` is not empty and `T` is `S` followed by

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-16-send-confirmation · **Version:** viola-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-16T04:48:16Z
- **Base commit:** `86fc64d0b4fb`, HEAD when P4 wrote this plan. Every git read below names it.

- **Inputs:**
  - `inputs#I1` — the overseer's phase directive.
  - `inputs#I2` — the P4 forks and their answers (the delegate overseer's, relayed by the operator; the founder away).

- **Founder's word owed:** Q1 of `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-16T04-10-47-phase/founder-forks.md`. The delegate answered
  «trailing whitespace only», PROVISIONAL. It is a boundary widening (playbook `rul-r74hshif`, `rul-p2zl2kgl`), so the
  wrap escalates it in the plain «Boundary widening» form. The candidate «either end» waits there for his return.

- **Live starts:** none, the cap 0 (`inputs#I2`). Every clause is proved on the fake agent. The tolerance accepts the
  untrimmed text too, so no clause rests on what the CLI trims.

A driver's send whose text the CLI submits with a trailing run of whitespace removed is read back as the driver's
own. Its `prompt-submitted` is relabelled `driver`, the send is confirmed, and the wheel stays with the driver. Today
the exact compare at `src/run/send/slot.rs:83` misses it. The line is then filed `human` and takes the wheel, and
the send ends exit 13. Every later send is refused until a `release` (`inputs#I1`, measured on 2.1.296).

The tolerance is the narrowest one `inputs#I2` answered: the claim takes the submitted text `S` when `S` equals the
typed text `T`, or when `S` is not empty and `T` is `S` followed only by whitespace. Nothing else changes:

- The text is still validated as received and typed as today (`typed_text`), and nothing is stripped. The logged
  line keeps the submitted text as it came, and `send-issued` keeps its `text_bytes`.
- A refused character is still refused (security-plan · decision/reject-dont-strip-paste-text).
- A human's different prompt still takes the wheel (architecture · decision/human-prompt-confirms-wheel-take).
- The local-command list still reads the exact typed text (architecture · decision/local-commands-by-ledger).
- Harness classification still reads the raw start (security-plan · decision/harness-prefix-literals).

The rule lives in one function of `viola-agent-claude` (architecture · decision/claude-shapes-isolated), so «either
end» is one additive line should the founder give it.

The readiness-gate turn race is closed for every turn the wrapper can know of. Two reads already cover the gate's
own wait: `src/run/send.rs:121-130` read the wheel and the turn again once the gate returns ready. What is left open
comes after those reads: the link record, `send-issued` and the paste (`src/run/send.rs:131-137`) follow with
nothing re-reading the turn. The fix runs those reads, the link, `send-issued` and the paste as one section under
the slot's flight lock. The hook's own claim, turn start and human wheel move take that same lock in
`append_hook_event`. A `prompt-submitted` the wrapper takes before the paste then refuses the send `turn-running`
with nothing typed. One taken after it belongs to a turn that began after the text went in.

Still beyond reach: a turn the CLI has started whose `UserPromptSubmit` has not yet reached the wrapper. Its hook
latency is unmeasured. It is named in v2-19's notes, and «Standing live rig with a screen model» owns its reading
(`inputs#I2`).

1. **The predicate (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`, beside `typed_text`).**
   - Add `pub const SUBMIT_TRIM: [char; 4]`: ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF.
   - Add `pub fn is_submitted_form(typed: &str, submitted: &str) -> bool`. It is true when `submitted == typed`. It is
     also true when `submitted` is not empty and `typed` with its trailing run of `SUBMIT_TRIM` characters removed
     equals `submitted`. Nothing else is true.
   - Its doc comment states three things:
     - The set is an assumption. The CLI's own trim set is not read from its bundle this chunk (`inputs#I2`).
     - The trailing side alone is the delegate's PROVISIONAL answer.
     - «either end» would be one more alternative in the same function.
   - It allocates nothing beyond what the compare needs, and reads no file.

3. **The claim (`src/run/send/slot.rs`).**
   - `SendSlot::claim` compares through `viola_agent_claude::hook::is_submitted_form(&f.text, text)` in place of
     `f.text == text`. The rest of its guard (a send that waits for a prompt, still `Waiting`) is unchanged.
   - The claim, the `session-start` claim (`session_started`), the turn start or end, and the unsent-human wheel move
     in `append_hook_event` are decided under ONE flight guard. That guard is released before the snapshot update and
     the append. Today each takes the lock on its own, and the turn and wheel moves take none.
   - The lock order stays flight before the wheel's `held` (as at `src/run/send.rs:102-103`). No path takes `held`
     then flight.
   - The relabel writes `origin: "driver"` alone. The line's `text` stays the submitted text.

4. **The guarded section (`src/run/send.rs`).**
   - Split `send` into the public `send` and a private `send_through(slot, name, instance_dir, call, window)`.
     `window: impl FnOnce(&SendSlot)` is called once after the gate returns ready, before the guarded section. `send`
     passes a no-op. This is a forced-window parameter (test-plan · decision/forced-window-hook-is-test-parameter):
     no env read, no feature, no seam.
   - The post-gate human-typing and turn-running reads move inside one `slot.flight()` guard. That guard is held
     across the link record, the `send-issued` append and the paste, and dropped right after the paste returns.
   - A refusal from those reads drops the guard first. It is then recorded as today: no cursor, no link, no
     `send-issued`, nothing typed.
   - The refusal order is unchanged (architecture · contract/refusal-order/send). The reads are the same two, made
     under the lock.
   - The confirmation window after the paste waits as today, with the guard released.
   - A second `send` arriving while the guard is held waits at its own arrival read (`src/run/send.rs:102`) until
     the paste returns. It then reads the first send in flight and is refused `not-delivered` / `turn-running`,
     nothing typed: the same answer it gets today.
   - A hook line arriving meanwhile waits the same way, at most the link, the `send-issued` append and the paste.
   - A human key never waits on it: the stdin path takes no flight lock.

5. **The race cases (`src/run/send.rs` tests, with a helper in `src/run/send/test_support.rs`).**
   - A helper sends `"hello"` through `send_through` to a quiet-gated slot over a tempdir instance and returns the
     reply, the dir and the pastes. Its window closure receives the slot.
   - `send_a_turn_started_after_the_post_gate_window_is_turn_running_and_types_nothing`: the window appends a
     `prompt-submitted` filed `harness` through `append_hook_event`. The reply is
     `{"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"turn-running"}`. The kinds read `["prompt-submitted","send-refused"]`, the
     refusal carries no cursor, and the pastes are empty.
   - `send_a_human_prompt_after_the_post_gate_window_is_human_typing_and_types_nothing`: the same with a prompt filed
     `human`. The reply is `{"refusal":"human-typing","detail":null}` and the pastes are empty.
   - Both are synchronous: no thread and no channel wait, so neither can hang past a failure (`inputs#I1` item 4).
   - With the guarded turn read removed, the first reads red: the text is pasted (the `locked-turn-read` control,
     step 10).

6. **The relabel cases (`src/run/send/relabel.rs`).**
   - An rstest table `send_a_prompt_the_cli_trimmed_at_the_end_is_relabelled_driver_and_confirmed`. The tails are a
     space, a tab, three spaces, and a space-tab-space. Each case:
     - sends `"run the skill"` with that tail and reads back a `prompt-submitted` of `"run the skill"` filed `human`;
     - expects the reply `ok`, the line relabelled `driver` with its text unchanged, and no `wheel` record;
     - expects the wheel holder `driver` afterwards.
   - `send_a_prompt_trimmed_at_the_start_claims_nothing`: typed `" run"`, read back `"run"` filed `human`. The line
     stays `human`, the wheel moves, and the window ends `no-prompt-submitted`. This pins the PROVISIONAL narrowness.
   - The three existing `claims_nothing` cases (relabel.rs:76, :124, :165) stay unchanged and green.
   - The cases reuse `test_support` (`confirmed_as`, `prompt`, `kinds`) and keep tests S3 and S4.

7. **The fake agent's trimmed submit (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/test_cases_opts.rs`).**
   - An argv flag `--trim-prompt-end`, parsed beside `--suppress-prompt-submit` (fake-agent.rs:128).
   - With it, a default `UserPromptSubmit`'s `prompt` field is the typed text with its trailing run of space, TAB,
     CR and LF removed. The receipt's `prompt` line keeps the typed text.
   - Off by default: every recorded-fixture comparison (`contract_fake_agent_drift`) is unchanged.
   - A parse case `opts_parse_reads_the_trim_prompt_end_flag` in `test_cases_opts.rs`.
   - Argv alone, no env read (test-plan · decision/fake-agent-argv-only; security-plan ·
     decision/new-env-read-needs-log-entry).

8. **The booted case (`tests/cli_send.rs`).**
   - `send_ending_in_whitespace_the_cli_trims_is_read_back_and_keeps_the_wheel`, booted as
     `boot(Some(PATH3), &["--trim-prompt-end"])` after the pattern at `tests/cli_send.rs:628`.
   - It sends `"{CANARY} run the skill  \t\n"` under `--json` and expects:
     - exit 0 and the `ok` document with `submitted_at` and `cursor`;
     - after the cursor: `send-issued`, a `prompt-submitted` with `origin: "driver"` and the text
       `"{CANARY} run the skill"`, then `send-confirmed`, and no `wheel` record.
   - It then ends the turn (`end_turn`) and sends again. The second send exits 0: the wheel stayed with the driver.
   - Waits come from the shared helpers under the 12 s `WITHIN` bound (test-plan · decision/within-7s-wait-bound).
     Keeps tests S1–S5.

9. **No other surface moves.** The MCP `send` tool and the CLI `send` read the wrapper's reply as today. `wait`'s
   wake rule, the dialog paths, the local-command list and `typed_text` are untouched. No recorded fixture is added or
   changed: the trimmed payload is the fake agent's, built from the typed text (tests S4).

10. **The controls (implement's one-shot runs, never entries).** Each is fired `gate.py control --timeout 120` on its
    filtered entry. The control id is ≤ 16 characters. «holds» means the named case ran and FAILED with no `TIMEOUT`
    line (`inputs#I1` item 3).
    - `trail-trim`:
      - edit: in `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs`, `is_submitted_form`'s trailing-run alternative removed,
        leaving `submitted == typed`;
      - case: `send_a_prompt_the_cli_trimmed_at_the_end_is_relabelled_driver_and_confirmed`, on entry 7.
    - `locked-turn-read`:
      - edit: in `src/run/send.rs`, the guarded turn-running read removed;
      - case: `send_a_turn_started_after_the_post_gate_window_is_turn_running_and_types_nothing`, on entry 6.
    - `fake-trim`:
      - edit: in `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, the `--trim-prompt-end` arm's trim removed (the prompt sent whole);
      - case: `send_ending_in_whitespace_the_cli_trims_is_read_back_and_keeps_the_wheel`, on entry 9. Its assertion
        of the relabelled text `"{CANARY} run the skill"` fails when the fake agent submits the untrimmed text, so the
        booted case proves it ran against a trimmed submit, not an exact one.
- none
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs` — `SUBMIT_TRIM`, `is_submitted_form`, its tables and property
- `src/run/send/slot.rs` — the claim through the predicate; one flight guard over the claim and the turn and wheel moves
- `src/run/send.rs` — `send_through` with its window; the post-gate reads, link, `send-issued` and paste under one guard; the race cases
- `src/run/send/relabel.rs` — the trimmed-prompt cases
- `src/run/send/test_support.rs` — the window helper
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — `--trim-prompt-end`
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/test_cases_opts.rs` — its parse case
- `tests/cli_send.rs` — the booted trimmed send

- **Not run: mutation.** No `run --mutants` (`inputs#I1` item 3). Each guard's strength is its one-shot control
  (step 10). A control mutates source, so it is no entry.
- **Not run: live legs.** No live `claude` start (`inputs#I2`: the cap is 0).

- **No smoke.** No boot-path touchpoint changes. `src/cmd/run.rs`, the plugin files and the start path are
  untouched, and the booted case boots its wrapper itself.

- **Why CI is read.** The operator pass pushes the chunk's tree and reads its run on CI's one leg, `ubuntu-latest`.
  The diff has no OS-conditional site, so no other leg is owed.
- **Base commit.** Git reads name `86fc64d0b4fb`.

## 2026-11-16-send-confirmation — 7. Test Data & Fixtures: 1 row(s)

**Change:** ~ contract/fake-agent-input/bracketed-paste · promise: was «Bracketed pastes plus Enter are accepted as one prompt and fire UserPromptSubmit (variant default) with that text.»; now «Bracketed pastes plus Enter are accepted as one prompt and fire UserPromptSubmit (variant default) with that text, or under --trim-prompt-end with its trailing run of space, TAB, CR and LF removed.»
**Why:** contract/fake-agent-input/bracketed-paste: The fake agent gained the argv flag --trim-prompt-end, which changes the prompt a default UserPromptSubmit fires with.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-16T05-15-05-wrap/

- `hook` module (as landed): `HookEvent` (10 registered events, `StopFailure` among them, the dialog tier `PreToolUse` / `PermissionRequest` included; `from_arg`, `kind()` — an `Option<EventKind>`, `None` for the dialog tier — `is_dialog()`, `as_str` = diag-line `$defs.hook_event`), `normalise(event, bytes) -> Normalised{kind, data, drift}` (StopFailure (`viola hook stop-failure`) maps to `turn-ended`, not a dialog, its data exactly `last_assistant_message` null, `background_tasks` null and `cause` `api-error`; Stop's `turn-ended` data is `{last_assistant_message, background_tasks}`, with no `cause`: `background_tasks` the payload array's length only, no element read or carried, `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array). A wrong-typed known field → a drift entry `{path, expected:"string"}` and read as absent. Prompt order: classify `harness` on the RAW prefix, no trim (`HARNESS_PREFIXES`: `<agent-message from=` / `<task-notification>` / `<\cross-session-message` / `<cross-session-message` — the escaped cross-session form is the one escaped tag that classifies; as measured on 2.1.287 a real cross-session message arrived unescaped under `from` / `from-name` / `from-mode`, and a `<task-notification>` typed at a prompt's very start arrives as typed and is filed `harness`), then unwrap only the CLI's unescaped same-id pair `<pasted_content id="X">\n…\n</pasted_content id="X">` together with the frame the CLI writes around it (the two newlines directly before the open tag, the one directly after the close tag, and a second after it when text follows that is not the next pair's own two-newline frame; a third before, a second after at the prompt's end and a lone one before stay, an unmatched open tag removes nothing; one id serves every pair of a session), then un-escape `<\` before an ASCII letter or `/` — a typed pair is never unwrapped. A pasted text's last newline never reaches the hook (measured on 2.1.287, wrapped or not), so `text` lacks it. No `send` relies on this: `typed_text(text)` returns a sent text with every CR LF pair as one LF, every other CR as one LF, and without its trailing CR and LF characters, every one of them in any order (a `Cow<'_, str>`, borrowed unless an inner CR is replaced; it holds no CR, and nothing else changes: not a TAB, a space, or an LF that is not at the very end), and the root bin's `send` types and classifies that typed text and matches a `prompt-submitted` text equal to it, or non-empty and equal to it less its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF (provisional), the text kept as submitted; the client's `refusal_of` is its second product caller (the founder's rulings, 2026-10-07T15:21Z for a trailing LF, 2026-10-09 for a trailing CR and CRLF, 2026-10-09T16:51Z for a CR or a CR LF inside; architecture [Delivery Confirmation]). An LF typed inside a paste is submitted unchanged (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text); every multi-line `send` relies on it, and it is gated by the ledger row `paste-newline` and its `viola verify` probe, Run B's `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (landed at chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row, stamped on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host). The frame beside typed text and between two pairs is unit-held and unprobed (`viola verify` types only lone pastes), and no probe is owed: a shape no `send` relies on needs none (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-07). StopFailure is registered, provisionally, with no ledger row and no verify probe.

- Wheel / dialog rules as in arch: `send` during a running turn → `turn-running` (a send's post-gate section — the human-typing and turn-running reads, the link record, `send-issued` and the paste — runs under one wrapper flight lock that the `hook.event` claim, turn start and end and wheel moves also take, a human key never; the turn lives in memory in `WheelSlot` beside holder and cause: `append_hook_event` marks it on a `prompt-submitted` of any origin and ends it on `turn-ended` / `session-start` / `session-end` before the line is appended; only a `release` that returns a human-held wheel clears it; a human prompt takes the wheel, so the send after it reads `human-typing`); `pause` → `manual-pause`; only CLI `release` returns the wheel; a pending dialog is answered `null` at once when the wheel moves to the human.

- **Wrapper:** `src/run/` (pump, wheel, gate wiring; `gate.rs` the bounded feed + `Gate`; `agents.rs` the bounded `claude agents --json` read (`read_logged`, `read_here`) shared by `list`, `revive`, verify's Run B and the `mcp` `list` tool (through `list::board_document`); `send.rs` the `send` module root — the `send` method on `Ctx` with its refusal order, re-exporting `SendSlot`, `append_hook_event` and `parse_from` —, one in flight with the remembered session id, the text validated as received and then typed with every inner CR or CR LF as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF (`typed_text`, the one text the list, the match, `text_bytes` and the paste read; an empty typed text is refused `empty-text` before the first wheel read, and by the client's `refusal_of` in `src/cmd/send.rs` before any frame), and its phases under `send/`: `slot.rs` the one-in-flight `SendSlot`, `append_hook_event` with the driver relabel (a `prompt-submitted` that is the typed text, or a non-empty text equal to it less its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF, appended with `origin:"driver"`, its text kept as submitted) and the `session-start` post-condition claim; `classify.rs` the local-command decision over `LOCAL_COMMANDS` (`classify`); `params.rs` `parse` / `parse_from`; and beside `send.rs` in `src/run/`: `wait.rs` the `WaitFeed` — the append under its lock, the Condvar wake, the newest turn and its start rebuild (which also returns the highest `dialog_id`), `appending_dialog` / `dialog_settled` — and the `wait` / `last` methods; `dialog.rs` the `DialogSlot` — the `hook.dialog` and `answer` methods, one pending dialog, the Condvar await on the injected clock up to the instance's dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, a `DialogHold` of whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, read once at the wrapper's start through `run::dialog::read_hold`), at whose end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line (`{dialog_id, dialog_kind}`, `source: wrapper`) through `WaitFeed::appending`, waking a parked `wait`, the per-tool armed continuation matched on equal `tool_input`; `wheel.rs` the `WheelSlot` — holder + cause under one lock, the synchronous in-memory move, the record worker (the `wheel` event, the snapshot, `run.wheel_transition`, the pending-dialog hand-back) flushed ≤ 2 s at exit before the terminal leaves raw mode, the stdin observer `Observed` and the F-W2 `Classifier`, and the `pause` / `release` methods; `snapshot.rs` the `Snapshots` holder every snapshot write goes through)

- SessionStart → `session-start` (`cause` startup|clear|resume|compact|unknown, `agent_session_id`); UserPromptSubmit → `prompt-submitted` (`text` normalised: long-paste wrapper removed, then tag escaping reversed; `origin` driver|human|harness — the hook files only human|harness, and `driver` comes only from the wrapper's relabel of the in-flight send's own prompt, matched on the send's typed text, the sent text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters, or on a non-empty text equal to that typed text less its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF, the text kept as submitted); PreToolUse AskUserQuestion → `question`; PreToolUse ExitPlanMode → `plan`; PermissionRequest → `permission` (a PermissionRequest repeating the armed `question` / `plan` dialog's tool with an equal `tool_input` is that dialog's continuation and raises no event); Stop → `turn-ended` (`last_assistant_message` or `null`; `background_tasks`, the Stop payload's `background_tasks` array length, a count only, or `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array); StopFailure (`viola hook stop-failure`) → `turn-ended`, not a dialog (data exactly `last_assistant_message` null, `background_tasks` null and `cause` `api-error`); SessionEnd → `session-end`; Notification / PostToolUse / PostToolUseFailure → `activity`.

- `RefusalReason` (kebab-case): `human-typing` · `unverified-cli` · `not-delivered` · `unknown` (`#[serde(other)]`; by design a code word outside the closed list stays visible in the document and in `refused: <word>`, and its exit is `unknown`'s 14 by `reason_of`). Details are closed per reason (`unknown`'s a code word or null, a code word being `viola_core::is_code_word`'s 1 to 64 bytes of `[a-z0-9-]`, a lower-case letter first); `reply_of` and `of_reply` read a `refusal` that is no code word as `unknown`, a string `detail` that is no code word as `null`, and a non-string `detail` as no known reply; `control-character` and then `empty-text` (an empty typed text on `send`) precede the documented order (`send`: human-typing → turn-running → input-not-ready → no-prompt-submitted, with human-typing and turn-running read a second time once the readiness gate's wait has returned ready, before anything is issued or typed, that post-gate section (the second reads, the link record, `send-issued` and the paste) running under the one wrapper flight lock the `hook.event` claim, turn start and end and wheel moves also take, a human key never taking it; `answer`: human-typing → unverified-cli → unknown-dialog). `unconfirmable` only ever appears inside an `ok` payload.

**"Strip-bay handoff, read back."** The direction the CLI carries, and the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) inherits, is an air-traffic-control tower strip bay after dark. Buff paper strips sit in anthracite holder boots on ruled aluminium racks, and every session keeps its slot for life. The only warm light is the one amber arrival holder cocked out of line when a session needs you. The voice is standard phraseology: short fixed words (`open`, `RB`, `unable`, `human-typing`, `not-delivered`), no filler, no guessing. Nothing announces success before it is confirmed: a send stays `open` until the matching `prompt-submitted` reads it back (its prompt equal to the sent text or, provisionally, to it with a trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR or LF removed; any leading or inner difference leaves it unconfirmed) (on a verified CLI, for `/clear` until its new-session post-condition does and for `/compact` until its same-session compact post-condition does; on an unverified CLI both `/clear` and `/compact` stay `unconfirmable`). Missing readings print `unknown`. It is explicitly NOT a monitoring dashboard: no status dots, toasts, graphs, spinners or glow.

- `validate_paste_text` allows LF/CR/TAB (multi-line relays are normal), rejects the rest — reject, never strip a refused character. Only allowed characters are rewritten or removed: after validation `send` types the text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters, and the delivery confirmation, the local-command list, `text_bytes` and the paste read that typed text (delivery is confirmed when the submitted text equals the typed text exactly, or is non-empty and equals it with its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF removed; no other difference, leading trimming included, is tolerated — provisional), which holds no CR (the founder's rulings, 2026-10-07T15:21Z for a trailing LF, 2026-10-09 for a trailing CR and CRLF, 2026-10-09T16:51Z for a CR or a CR LF inside). An empty typed text is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (exit 13), by the client before any frame and by the wrapper before the first wheel read.

- `validate_paste_text` over decoded `char`s: allow LF/CR/TAB, refuse every other C0, DEL and C1 with `not-delivered` / `control-character` — reject, never strip a refused character. After validation the wrapper's `send` types the text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters (`viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text`; it holds no CR, only CR and LF are rewritten or removed, and no refused character is typed or removed), and the delivery confirmation, the local-command list, `text_bytes` and the paste read that typed text (delivery is confirmed when the submitted text equals the typed text exactly, or is non-empty and equals it with its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF removed; no other difference, leading trimming included, is tolerated — provisional). An empty typed text, the empty text included, is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (exit 13) right after `control-character`: by the client before any frame and by the wrapper before the first wheel read.

- **Path 2 — confirmed `send` + CL-1 records** — `cursor` = pre-paste offset, `send-issued` then `prompt-submitted{driver}` holding the submitted text (the typed text, or the typed text less the trailing run of space, TAB, CR and LF the CLI trimmed);
